does_not_weaken_the_hypothesis: A floor-effect null is not evidence against a mechanism. The hypothesis remains untested.
established_anyway: rt.promote() works on macOS and the daemon does not call it
linux-x1's finding that host/daemon/ contains zero calls reproduces as a code fact on a second bench
whether the daemon should promote is a design question that outlives #58, since it is true at idle as well
hypothesis_from: linux-x1: the contention route is scheduling latency on an unpromoted reader. host/daemon/ contains zero calls to rt.promote().
not_run_here: The 2x arm. It requires deliberately saturating an interactive workstation and the bench owner asked for it to stop - 16 busy loops on 8 cores ran the fan at full for several minutes and they had not been warned beforehand. Handed to linux-x1, whose bench reaches 2x routinely and where the baseline fires at 8/18 so an effect would be visible.
the_design_did_work: Per-run wall times were 11.5 s in the unpromoted arm and 11.6 s in the promoted arm, so both were genuinely and equally loaded. That per-run load witness is what distinguishes this floor effect from the three arms spoiled earlier today by load that had already stopped.
why_inconclusive: The baseline never failed, so there was nothing for promotion to improve. Earlier 1x arms on this bench read 5/14; this one read 0/12. That spread is the variance at 1x, which is why linux-x1's sweep puts the usable threshold at 2x.
why_this_bench: rt.promote() returns Operation not permitted in their session (ulimit -r is 0). It works here: qos=user-interactive, time-constraint 5/0.5/2.5 ms.
